title: VTC in mimid: carry the SDP in the call room, which authenticates it and makes the 1:1 demo need no media key
description:
From reading MarkAtwood/ParlorVTC on 2026-11-23 at Mark's suggestion.
Parlor is a 1:1 asymmetric voice queue: two HTML files, no server, no
build step, ~1100 lines of ES modules, WebRTC P2P voice, and signalling
over public Nostr relays.

THE IDEA WORTH TAKING. Parlor carries the WebRTC offer, answer and ICE
candidates inside NIP-04 encrypted direct messages (NIP-PARLOR.md
"Queue and Signaling Messages (kind:4)"): the relay carries signalling it
cannot read, and the media never touches it. The analogue for mimid is
exact and better: carry the SDP as MIMI messages IN THE CALL ROOM. The
call room stops being only a key source and becomes the signalling
channel, which it is already suited to -- E2EE, ordered by the hub,
fanned out to exactly the call's members and nobody else.

WHAT MIMI GETS THAT PARLOR CANNOT HAVE. Parlor's SPEC §Authentication
says "All Nostr events are signed with sender's Ed25519 key... No
additional authentication layer needed", but a supplicant's key is
ephemeral and generated per session, and §Impersonation concedes
"Supplicants are anonymous by design". So the host cannot know who
called. In MIMI the SDP travels inside the MLS group, so THE DTLS
FINGERPRINTS IN IT ARE AUTHENTICATED BY MLS, bound to the sender's
credential identity. No short authentication string, no reading a
fingerprint aloud. draft-atwood-jmap-vtc's e2eeFingerprint field and
jmap-vtc-e2ee-guide.md §8 "Fingerprint verification" are both
unnecessary for a MIMI-backed call, because MLS has already done it.
That is a demonstrable advantage and belongs in the draft.

AND IT REORDERS THE BUILD. WebRTC peer-to-peer is DTLS-SRTP, which is
already end-to-end encrypted between two peers. So a 1:1 call needs NO
media_secret, NO SFrame and NO SFU: SDP over MIMI messages plus WebRTC is
a working, authenticated, end-to-end encrypted call. media_secret is
needed when media passes through an SFU, which is the GROUP case.

That means the shortest path to the demo is SIGNALLING, not keying, and
we built keying first (bead mimid-1wgh.108). Not wasted -- it is what
makes the group case work and it is what draft-atwood-mimi-calls is
about -- but the 1:1 demo is reachable sooner than the build order on
decision mimid-1wgh.113 implies.

WHERE THE SDP GOES, and it is spec-correct rather than a repurposing.
mimi-content-10 §5.10: "a description of a multimedia session, or a URI
used to join one". Everything so far has used the SECOND half, the join
URI (bead mimid-1wgh.114.3). The FIRST half is the slot for SDP, and
nobody has used it. mimid already anticipates it and declines: our
content.rs says "Any other inline session description (SDP, say) is left
out", and draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi-00 §Calls says such a part "maps to
no MessageAction, because JMAP Chat has no field for one". So the
container exists, we already parse around it, and using it is the
opposite of the mimi:// mistake of bead mimid-1wgh.114.1.

THE PART THAT CANNOT BE PEER-TO-PEER: TURN. Parlor hardcodes Jami's
public servers with the credentials ring/ring, and its SPEC is straight
about the consequence -- "TURN servers know: IP addresses of call
participants, that encrypted bytes are flowing". For mimid that is a
deployment configuration item and a Security Considerations line, and it
is the one third party no amount of MLS removes.

SHAPE WORTH COPYING: no build step, no dependencies, no npm, runs from
file://. A mimid demo client could be the same -- a static page speaking
JMAP to the local agent and WebRTC to the peer. That does not breach
decision mimid-1wgh.38 (mimid ships no UI) if it lives in its own repo or
as a test fixture rather than inside mimid.

WHAT PARLOR DOES NOT SOLVE: groups. It is one host and a queue of
visitors, one call at a time, so it never needs a group key and never
faces the problem draft-atwood-mimi-calls exists for. The MLS work is
exactly where Parlor stops.

DECISION FOR MARK: whether signalling goes before keying in the build
order, and whether the SDP-in-§5.10 mapping goes into
draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi §Calls, which currently says we map no
session description at all.
notes:
THE SPEC HALF IS WRITTEN 2026-11-23, two commits HELD UNPUSHED in
jmap-chat-spec pending Mark:
- 59e362c, draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi-00 §Calls: an inline session part
  of content type application/sdp is call signalling. A converting party
  MUST NOT put it in a Message body or map it to a MessageAction, and in
  a call room delivers it to the VTC capability. Cites RFC8866 for SDP
  and RFC8122 for the fingerprint attribute.
- 4b1c3ee, draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00: the surface that commit refers to.

WHY TWO COMMITS AND WHY HELD: 59e362c alone referred to a VTC capability
that did not exist. The VTC draft's own Explicit Non-Prescriptions said
"SDP offer/answer and ICE candidate exchange are the media stack's
responsibility. A future companion specification may define JMAP-based
signaling relay, but this document does not." So the binding promised a
delivery target the other draft declined to define. Caught one tool call
after committing it; Mark chose to hold rather than soften the sentence.

WHAT 4b1c3ee ADDS:
- VTCCall/signal, one session description or ICE candidate out. Not a
  standard JMAP method; a client holding a call SHOULD use the WebSocket
  transport, since trickled candidates beat an HTTP round trip each. An
  unregistered signal type is refused rather than dropped, so a client
  learns the server will not carry it instead of finding a call that
  never connects. rateLimit rather than a silent drop, because a dropped
  candidate looks exactly like one that found no route.
- VTCCallSignal, one in. Ephemeral, never in a /get or /query, never
  replayed. participantId comes from the AUTHENTICATED MLS SENDER, not
  from anything the sender asserted.
- The ordering property: the room's hub orders what it accepts, so offer
  and answer arrive in order with no sequence numbers of ours.
- The authentication property, which is the valuable one: the fingerprints
  in a session description are bound to the sender's credential, so a
  MIMI-signalled call needs no fingerprint comparison and e2eeFingerprint
  is for calls signalled otherwise.
- That a 2-party call then needs NO exported secret, which is the build
  order change on decision mimid-1wgh.113.
- supportsMimiKeyedCalls renamed supportsMimiCalls, since it now gates
  the room, its signalling and its keying. The old name shipped in
  fb05ead, which is pushed; the rename is in this commit.
- The WebRTC-signalling non-prescription rewritten to say this document
  now does relay it for a call with a MIMI room.
- §NAT Traversal Is Not Negotiated and §Call Signalling Is Visible to the
  Whole Call, below.

TURN, Mark 2026-11-23: "maybe mimid needs to run a TURN server, or
endpoints have to negotiate which TURN server to use, but that cant get
baked into the specs themselves". He is right and the draft already
agreed -- STUN/TURN deployment was already an Explicit Non-Prescription.
The resolution written in: which relay a client uses is between that
client AND ITS OWN PROVIDER, never between the two ends of a call. Each
end offers the candidates its own provider gave it and ICE agrees a pair,
so nothing crosses the interop boundary. The exposure argument: a
client's own provider already knows its address because the client
connects to it, so relaying there tells it nothing new; a relay at the
other end learns an address and that bytes flow, not whose call it is;
and pointing BOTH ends at one third-party relay hands that third party
both addresses and the fact that those two parties spoke, which media
encryption does not take back. That last is what Parlor does, with
Jami's servers and the credentials ring/ring.

WHETHER MIMID RUNS ONE is deployment and ops, not spec: ship coturn or
document it. Not filed as spec work.

THE MESH LIMITATION, stated rather than discovered later: a signal
reaches every member of the call's room because that is the granularity
at which MLS encrypts. Fine for 2-party and for an SFU that is itself a
participant. In a mesh call among three or more, the session description
meant for one peer is readable by all, and a client MUST NOT present such
a call as though signalling were private between pairs.

BUILDS CLEAN: kramdown-rfc exit 0, xml2rfc 0 errors, after adding
RFC8866, RFC8122, RFC4648 and a W3C WebRTC reference that xml2rfc caught
as unresolved IDREFs.
